pillar_reactions.evidence: Accepted the training logic quickly ('Oh, no, I believe that... No doubt') but interrogated the delivery: 'Videoing myself, training, sending, okay, if I commit something, I will do it, but it's definitely not something I like to do, because I don't like phones', then 'I know what I would be doing. How does he know what I'm doing?' The rep answered with the app mechanic and narrowed video submission to the learning phase, and the prospect withdrew it: 'is this a deal breaker over here, the phone? No, it's not.'

Said he had no questions in the moment ('No, not really') and volunteered that he already runs 18:6 intermittent fasting, but came back to it later with the real question: 'how is this program going to tell me what to eat, how much to eat, when to eat?' He also pushed back on the rep's framing that vegan protein is harder — 'I think it's also a myth. It's, it's because we're not used to that.' He ultimately ranked it as the pillar he needs least.

Named it as the reason he was on the call, unprompted, when asked to rank: 'out of the three blocks that you mentioned, the three, the third one is the one that I'm looking for.' Consistent with his own diagnosis earlier — 'for me, what works always the best is to have a plan, a plan, or a program, or routine.' The rep read this correctly going in: 'the last part is, I think, this is what you came here for, the structure and the accountability.'

anchors.raw: if I would compare it to what I had a personal trainer, with my membership, I paid 250 euros per month, and then I had every week a session with the trainer.
anchors.competitor: Former personal trainer, in person, weekly
anchors.note: His reference point for premium coaching is EUR 250/month all-in with a live weekly session. The offer is roughly four times that for asynchronous app-based coaching, and he made the comparison himself within seconds of hearing the number ('1,000 a month').

anchors.raw: Well, it's like 95, maybe, 95... 95 euros per month. So it's not like super, well, it's still, you know, it's almost 100 euros.
anchors.note: Contracted until February and not cancellable, so it runs in parallel with any purchase. He costed that explicitly against the offer: 'I will pay 600 euros also for my gym membership, which is 10% of that.'

anchors.raw: They asked for 16,000 euros for that. And I'm like, you've got to be kidding me. It's a customized, simple jacket. Like, where has this world gone to? ... you can make it for 2,000, 3,000, 4,000, 1,000. ... I'm not saying that this directly relates to that, okay, Trevor is just placed, he's the Miu Miu customized leather plus 12 jacket.
anchors.competitor: Prada / Miu Miu — used as an analogy, not a substitute
anchors.note: The most consequential anchor of the call and one that has no price tag on it. He develops product for a fashion brand and prices from cost to make; he applied that lens to Primal and concluded it is a margin play. 'I know exactly what it costs to make it, to develop it. And then I see things... and I'm thinking, this is so over the top.' Every price reduction the rep offered confirmed this thesis rather than answering it.

anchors.raw: It's not the price. No, but it's the only doubt I sent already a while back. I said, no, it's the price. It's not, he believes in himself. He's positioned himself high. He's confident. And he, I talk about Trevor, but it's also a brand. ... I think it's good, but I don't think we match.
anchors.note: He reads the price as a positioning statement rather than a value statement, and reads himself out of the target market on that basis. Combined with the AI messaging complaint, this is a marketing-side loss dressed as a price objection.

unmet_demand.want: The structure and programming pillar on its own, without paying for the nutrition and coaching layers he already covers himself
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a single bundled three-pillar package and the rep explicitly refused to unbundle: 'it is designed like this because it cannot be separate' and 'if you would be only doing workouts, like he wouldn't have such amazing results because the nutrition is a crucial part of the transformation.'

unmet_demand.want: A short, low-commitment way to try the coaching before committing thousands
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No trial exists in the stated offer. The rep invented one live at $1,200 or $1,500 for a month, which the prospect refused — 'Yeah, but something tells me no... My gut feeling. About what? About the price.' The improvised version arrived seventy minutes in and after three other prices, so it read as further discounting rather than as a product.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching delivered without a phone in his hand while he trains
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Delivery is app-based with video submission and tick-off tracking. The rep offered a laptop workaround but the mechanic is inherently screen-mediated. The prospect said it was not a deal breaker, so this is a friction, not a blocker — but it is a recurring theme for older, low-tech, high-income buyers.

unmet_demand.want: Communications that do not read as American hype or as AI-generated
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing about the product requires it — the objection is entirely to the marketing wrapper. 'I keep getting these messages, it actually turns me totally off... it's clearly AI, and I'm not a, you know, it's a bit of a turn off' and 'what he's built around it, I find not fully matching with what I thought he is about.' A qualified, solvent, product-convinced European buyer disqualified the brand on tone.
